items.stem: In most industrial control environments, which priority is typically ranked HIGHEST?

options.text: Safety and availability of the physical process
options.rationale: Correct: in OT, safety and keeping the process running are usually paramount.
Marketing confidentiality is not the primary OT concern.
This is unrelated to ICS priorities.
Unscheduled reboots threaten availability and are undesirable.

items.stem: What is the Purdue model mainly used for in ICS security?

options.text: Organising control system components into hierarchical levels and zones
options.rationale: Correct: the Purdue model structures ICS into levels to guide segmentation.
The Purdue model is an architectural reference, not an encryption tool.
It is not a workforce scheduling model.

items.stem: Select TWO challenges that make securing OT different from securing typical IT.

options.text: Legacy devices may not support modern patching or authentication
options.rationale: Correct: many OT devices are long-lived and cannot be easily patched.

options.text: Availability and safety often outweigh taking systems offline for updates
options.rationale: Correct: downtime can be unacceptable, constraining security actions.

options.text: OT environments always have the newest hardware
options.rationale: OT often runs long-lived legacy equipment, not the newest hardware.

options.text: Industrial protocols were all designed with strong built-in security
options.rationale: Many industrial protocols lack built-in authentication or encryption.

options.text: Safety is irrelevant in industrial settings
options.rationale: Safety is a central concern in industrial settings.

items.explanation: Correct: many OT devices are long-lived and cannot be easily patched.
